The expected number of games is about 29.99.

**Setup.** Let p = 0.3 (Frank wins a game) and q = 0.7 (Joe wins a game). A match ends when someone reaches 21 wins, so it lasts 21 + k games, where k ≤ 20 is the loser's win count.

E = Σₖ₌₀²⁰ (21+k) · C(20+k, k) · (q²¹pᵏ + p²¹qᵏ)

**Simplify.** Since (21+k)·C(20+k, k) = 21·C(21+k, k), each term has the form 21·C(21+k, k)·q²¹pᵏ. Multiplying and dividing by q gives a negative-binomial probability.

Σₖ₌₀²⁰ C(21+k, k) q²² pᵏ is the probability that Joe gets 22 wins before Frank gets 21 wins. That equals P(Bin(42, 0.7) ≥ 22). The Frank term is analogous.

So E = 21·[P(Bin(42, 0.7) ≥ 22)/0.7 + P(Bin(42, 0.3) ≥ 22)/0.3].

Let Y ~ Bin(42, 0.3). Then P(Bin(42, 0.7) ≥ 22) = P(Y ≤ 20) = 1 − P(Y ≥ 21). Writing T₂₁ = P(Y ≥ 21) and T₂₂ = P(Y ≥ 22):

E = 30(1 − T₂₁) + 70·T₂₂

**Numerics.**
- P(Y = 21) = C(42,21)·(0.21)²¹ ≈ 0.003145.
- The ratio P(k+1)/P(k) = ((42−k)/(k+1))·(3/7) gives P(22) ≈ 0.0012866, P(23) ≈ 0.00047948, P(24) ≈ 0.00016268, and so on.
- Summing the tail gives T₂₂ ≈ 0.0019976, so T₂₁ ≈ 0.005143.

E ≈ 30 − 30(0.005143) + 70(0.0019976) ≈ 30 − 0.1543 + 0.1398 ≈ 29.985

ANSWER: 29.985
